text: External fire near the equipment — External fire heats butadiene in spheres, causing thermal polymerization/decomposition, pressure increase, possible BLEVE or explosion.
Loss of cooling water — Cooling water stops flowing into column C-102, causing reflux to drop, temperatures to rise, and pressure to increase as boil-up intensifies.
Normal co‑presence in process line/equipment — Possible exothermic reaction between acetylene and butadiene generating heat and pressure, potentially releasing flammable gases.
Co‑location in same equipment/line (normal operation) — Mixing of saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons may produce an exothermic reaction, releasing heat and potentially causing overpressure.
Heating of water in line L-FEED or vessel V-101 (e.g., steam tracing, fire) — Water heated to steam, possible pressure increase if confined, could cause overpressure of adjacent equipment
No EPA 1980 listed reactive group pair for butadiene/butane interaction — 1,3-butadiene and butanes could meet in L-FEED line through wrong charge or transfer, potentially releasing flammable mixture
Piping leak — Water ingress into butadiene line could lead to unwanted reactions, corrosion or pressure changes.
No listed cause describes water contact — NMP may separate or form heterogeneous mixture with water; no EPA 1980 listed hazard codes for NMP-water pair

Startup recycle line L-STARTUP-RECYCLE left open, adding extra flow from pump discharge to column — Increased flow into column can cause flooding, entrainment of liquid in vapor, possible overpressure leading to relief valve RV-C104 actuation and release of butadiene to flare.

Product pump P-104A stops, eliminating flow through recycle line and product withdrawal — No flow through column stops reflux and reboiler circulation, leading to temperature/pressure excursions; overpressure or underpressure may trigger relief devices RV-C104 and/or RV-P104A, releasing butadiene to flare.
External fire near the equipment — Fire heating TOTES could increase internal pressure, potentially exceeding design pressure and causing rupture.
External fire or hot surface near tote heating the methylhydrogen siloxane fluid — Heating may cause Si-H bond cleavage, releasing hydrogen gas (flammable) and forming siloxanes.

Incorrect feed or cross‑contamination introducing an unintended chemical into the filling line. — Unintended chemical may accumulate, potentially causing hazardous reaction, product quality issues, or release if volatile.
Blockage downstream or valve closed causing pressure to rise in the filling line. — Overpressure could rupture the homogeniser/filling line, releasing process material into the building interior.

Loss of cooling or continued heating while circulation stopped, raising temperature in the line. — Elevated temperature could cause thermal decomposition, overpressure, or equipment failure, releasing hot material.
Incorrect feed or cross‑connection introducing a foreign substance into the line. — Incompatible material could react, generate gas or heat, causing overpressure or corrosion and release.
Operator charges incorrect material into mixing tank via hose — Wrong composition enters tank, leading to off-spec product, possible unsafe reaction or release if incompatible.

Temperature change causing phase change (e.g., heating leading to vaporization or cooling leading to solidification) — If the material changes phase, pressure could rise or flow could block, potentially causing hose rupture or pump deadhead and release of the material, exposing personnel.
External fire near the equipment — External fire near the hose/pump heats the contents, increasing temperature and pressure in the line and tank

Valve left in wrong position (operator or maintenance error) — Continued pumping with discharge blocked raises pressure in hose, potentially causing hose rupture or fitting failure and release of tank contents onto the warehouse floor.
